headline: Move twice as fast to identify the second middle
statement: Return the middle node of a nonempty singly linked list. For an even number of nodes, return the second of the two middle nodes.
intuition: Move a slow pointer one link and a fast pointer two links on every turn. When the fast pointer reaches the end, the slow pointer is halfway through the list. The loop condition makes an even-length list return the second of its two middle nodes.
approach: Start slow and fast at head.
While fast and fast.next exist, advance slow one link and fast two.
Return slow, preserving its original identity and suffix.
correctness: For odd n=2k+1 the loop runs k times and returns index k. For even n=2k it runs k times and returns index k, the second middle. No input links are modified.
bruteForce: Count nodes first, then walk floor(n/2) links in a second pass.

complexity.explanation: The two pointers traverse the list with no additional collection.

pitfalls: Use the loop condition that returns the second middle for even length.
Return the original node, not a newly constructed list with the same values.
